abstract: During oogenesis, the establishment of oocyte-specific gene expression relies on epigenetic and transcriptional remodeling. Both histone modifications and transcription factors are crucial for the oocyte to acquire developmental competence; however, the mechanisms involved remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify transcription factor 3 (TCF3), an E-protein family member, as a key maternal regulator of oocyte developmental potential. Oocyte-specific deletion of Tcf3 results in female infertility, characterized by impaired meiotic maturation and early embryonic arrest at the two-cell stage. These defects are associated with defective maternal mRNA clearance and disrupted establishment of the H3K4me3 landscape in maturing oocytes. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that TCF3 directs H3K4me3 deposition at target gene promoters through interaction with CXXC finger protein 1 (CXXC1), the core subunit of the SETD1 histone methyltransferase complex. Importantly, this TCF3-CXXC1 interaction depends on their DNA-binding activity, highlighting the specificity of TCF3 in coordinating with CXXC1 to regulate maternal target genes, such as Pabpn1l. Together, our findings uncover a transcription factor-driven mechanism of epigenetic reprogramming that is essential for the maternal-to-zygotic transition.
